_comment: Register-exclusion list for the maxDF* corpus-convergence metric. These are NEX5's OWN habitual vocabulary -- the words her crystallized voice uses regardless of subject. They are excluded so that maxDF* measures convergence onto an EXTERNAL topic, not the standing register. This list is FITTED DATA and it WILL DRIFT. Refit when 'fitted_on' is stale, and refit ONLY on a corpus with no active convergence in it.
method: document frequency over the corpus using _fidelity_tokens() from crystallizer.py (GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md section 1: lowercase, strip possessives, drop <3 chars, drop furniture); take the top 40 by DF
stability_check: refitting with the last 7 or 14 days withheld keeps 33/40 terms and leaves the backtest quantiles identical (12/18/22%), so the metric is not sensitive to the exact tail of this list

correction.what: Removed 2 of the original 40 terms: 'changes' and 'systems'.
correction.why: This list was fitted 2026-06-20..2026-08-04, a window that spans the 'Gatwick' exemplar-pool contamination (fires 2026-07-26..2026-08-07, crystallized beliefs 2026-07-28..2026-08-08). That violates this file's own header rule -- 'refit ONLY on a corpus with no active convergence in it'. Three contaminant tokens sat in the 40: changes, shifts, systems. Measured against a clean pre-contamination corpus (2026-06-01..2026-07-28, n=1627, 0 contaminant): 'changes' DF 0.0080 and 'systems' DF 0.0197, NEITHER in a clean top-40 -- they entered this list only because of the contamination, and excluding them blinds maxDF* to any future convergence driven by them. 'shifts' was KEPT: DF 0.0301 clean, rank 37 in a clean fit, so it is genuine standing register.
correction.measured_effect_on_readings: NONE. Replaying maxDF* daily over 2026-07-01..2026-08-10 with and without these two terms gives an identical breach history (1 breach day, peak 30.0% on 08-04 driven by 'societal') and an identical mean live reading (19.5%). The contamination of this list was real but INERT: the tokens it wrongly absorbed never drove a reading. This correction buys future sensitivity, not a changed past.
correction.what_was_NOT_done: A full refit was rejected on measurement. A clean corpus large enough for a stable 40-term fit exists (2026-06-01..2026-07-28, n=1627; bootstrap shows ~1000 docs needed for R31's 33/40 stability bar), but it is entirely PRE-R29. Refitting on it is a REGRESSION for live use: it drops 'emerging' (DF 0.0246 in that corpus but 0.1613 in the live post-R29 corpus), which then surfaces as a false driver and raises the mean live reading 19.5% -> 20.8%, closer to the 25% threshold. See observation_reports/r50.md A.3.
correction.the_defect_that_remains: STALENESS, not contamination, is this list's real problem, and it is NOT fixed here. R29 (2026-08-03) tripled crystallized-belief length: mean content tokens per document 9.6 pre-R29 vs 27.7 post. The current standing register is under-excluded -- 'aligns' (DF 0.1342) and 'discusses' (DF 0.1613) are in the live corpus at register-level frequency and appear in NO version of this list, which is why maxDF* now reads 18-24% with those as drivers. Fixing it needs ~1000 CLEAN POST-R29 documents; only 154 exist as of 2026-08-10, accruing ~78/day, so roughly 11 more clean days. Refit then, not before.

patch.what: PARTIAL PATCH -- added 4 post-R29 frame tokens: item, aligns, discusses, highlights. Nothing removed; the 38 v2 terms are unchanged.
patch.this_is_NOT_the_refit: The full 40-term refit that R50 deferred STILL HAS NOT HAPPENED and is still gated on a clean adequate corpus (~1,000 clean post-R29 documents; 575 exist as of 2026-08-21, projected ~2026-08-31 at the earliest -- see r73.md B). This patch only stops the metric false-alarming on its own prose in the meantime. Refit properly when the window opens; do not treat this file as a fitted list.
patch.why: R50 recorded staleness as this list's remaining defect and named 'aligns' and 'discusses' explicitly. R73 measured the consequence: maxDF* was reading 32.0% on 'item' and breaching on 11 of 13 days -- on NEX's own narration scaffold, not on any attractor. 'item' is the frame subject in 148 of 575 clean-window documents ('The item discusses...', 'This item states...'), with discusses/aligns/highlights as its verbs.
patch.selection_criterion: FRAME vocabulary (how NEX narrates) is excludable; CONTENT nouns (what she narrates about) are NOT, because a convergence onto a content noun is exactly what this metric exists to catch. Measured on the CLEAN post-R29 window 2026-08-09..2026-08-16 (n=575, both known contaminants under 5% every day), the frame family reads: item 28.9%, aligns 22.8%, discusses 17.4%, highlights 10.6%, then suggests 6.6%, underscores 5.4%, and everything else at or below 2.1%. The four added are exactly those that could plausibly drive a reading against a 25% threshold; the tail was left out deliberately -- excluding a token that cannot drive a reading buys nothing and only costs sensitivity.

guard_against_masking_a_real_attractor.test_1_backtest_unchanged: Replayed over R31's own fitted window (2026-06-20..2026-08-04, n=1101 reproduced exactly): v2 gives median 12% / p90 18% / p99 22% / max 26% / 1 breach, reproducing R31's recorded quantiles exactly. v3 gives IDENTICAL values. The patch does not alter a single historical reading, because these tokens entered NEX's voice after R29 and were not register-level in R31's corpus.
guard_against_masking_a_real_attractor.test_2_attractors_become_MORE_visible: On 08-20 v2 read 27.2% on 'item' while societal sat underneath at 24.7%; under v3 societal IS the driver. On 08-21 v2 read 37.8% on 'item' while advancements sat underneath; under v3 advancements IS the driver at 24.3%. The live rolling reading moves 32.0% ('item', BREACH) -> 24.0% ('advancements', no breach). The patch raises sensitivity to real attractors rather than lowering it.
guard_against_masking_a_real_attractor.test_3_none_of_the_four_is_an_attractor: Daily-DF burst ratio (max/median) and branch-distribution entropy relative to the corpus, 08-09..08-21: item 1.2/0.960, aligns 1.4/1.007, discusses 1.4/0.987, highlights 2.0/0.929 -- all flat and branch-agnostic. The two known attractors score societal 22.7/0.808 and advancements 3.8/0.803, the two lowest branch entropies of the 20 tokens tested. societal and advancements are NOT in this list and must never be added.

patch.measured_effect: Live rolling-50 reading 32.0% -> 24.0%; driver 'item' -> 'advancements'; breach clears. Over readings since 08-09: mean 31.6% -> 23.8%, max 46.0% -> 34.0%, breaching readings 878/1041 (84%) -> 383/1041 (37%).
patch.what_remains_broken: v3 still breaches on 37% of readings since 08-09, driven by CONTENT nouns that are themselves flat and branch-agnostic: systems (103 breach readings), engagement (86), foundation (46), dynamics (29). These are standing vocabulary in noun form and are deliberately NOT excluded here -- any of them could carry a genuine convergence. Note in particular that 'systems' was REMOVED from this list by R50 on pre-R29 evidence (clean DF 0.0197) and now reads 16.7% on the clean post-R29 window: R50's removal was correct on its evidence and is the single largest source of remaining breaches. That judgement belongs to the full refit, not to this patch. The metric still has thin headroom.
